constraint: No new runtime or benchmark dependency; use Python standard library and saved source data.

papers.title: MonetDB/X100: Hyper-Pipelining Query Execution
papers.lesson: Amortize interpretation overhead with bounded batches; excessive intermediate materialization and overlarge working sets can reverse gains.
papers.application_hypothesis: Batch metadata retrieval and reuse immutable preparation while retaining per-product evidence checks. Python batching does not imply the paper's native vectorization speedups.

papers.title: Cache-Conscious Data Structures
papers.read: Abstract and section 3 clustering/compression discussion; PDF text extraction partly garbled
papers.lesson: Group related records and reduce pointer-heavy working sets.
papers.application_hypothesis: Prebuilt compact records, lazy indexed reads and small hot caches may lower cold-start memory; measure rather than assume CPU-cache benefit in Python.

papers.title: PTHash: Revisiting FCH Minimal Perfect Hashing
papers.lesson: Static keys can map to compact dense identifiers, but the perfect-hash definition does not establish membership for unknown keys.
papers.application_hypothesis: Dense IDs and packed offsets may be worth testing; preserve exact key comparison for misses. No new PTHash library or custom production perfect-hash engine is proposed.

evidence_status: Research only. Paper-reported speedups are not Shopextract benchmark results. Actual bounded comparison is requested and pending current regression run.
